judges.reason: B's printed-slip concept carries through the layout, typography, and tactile link reveal, making the page feel more particular to this photographer than a conventional link list. A is polished and especially lean, but its visual language and interactions are more familiar. Both meet the listed hard gates.

baseline.notes: A is a restrained, coherent editorial layout with clear link rows and appropriate hover, focus, and press feedback. It stays lightweight, uses system fonts, includes a visible keyboard focus state, and provides a reduced-motion path. Its visual idea is less distinctive than B's.

skill.notes: The torn-edge slip and print-reveal interaction create a distinctive, consistent concept that suits the brief's small set of destinations. The display type gives it a strong identity, though the monospaced name may feel cramped at narrow widths. Keyboard focus, touch-sized rows, forced-colors handling, and reduced motion are addressed; extra font and image asset references make its performance less certain than A's.

judges.reason: B has a clear, ownable concept: the print slip and its print-head reveal run through the structure, the type and the interaction, so the page reads as hers rather than as a link-in-bio template. A is technically excellent and a bit lighter and more accessible, but it looks generic and leaves awkward empty space at 1440px. Neither fails a hard gate. B's lead on concept, originality and typography outweighs A's small edge on performance and brief fidelity.

baseline.notes: Clean, restrained link page. The 'contact sheet / shutter' idea shows up only in a code comment and in the rust press state; visually it reads as a well-made generic link list. System serif + sans + mono stack with no web font, so it is very light on 3G. Motion: ink plate wipes in from the left, arrow nudges (diagonal for mailto), rust 'shutter' press with a 1px sink. All have a reduced-motion path. Excellent a11y: skip link, focus-visible matches hover, forced-colors and dark-mode support, rows 72px+ tall, absolute URLs as briefed. Finished-looking framed placeholder at 4:5. Weaknesses: at 1440 the link column is bottom-aligned with a large empty area above it; on mobile a tall empty gap before the footer; the rust focus outline on the ink fill has low contrast (the fill change still makes focus clear); preload of portrait.jpg will 404 until the file arrives.

skill.notes: One clear idea carried throughout: a torn paper print slip/receipt (sawtooth edges on a dark 'table') where each link is a printed line and hover/focus/press runs a 'print head' clip-path reveal of an inverted copy. Contact is printed in rust. Martian Mono display face (font-display: swap, so text is not blocked) paired with a Charter serif bio and mono details. Distinctive and fits a documentary photographer's quiet, exact tone. Motion is purposeful, CSS only, with a reduced-motion path. Strong a11y: skip link, aria-hidden duplicate layer, inset focus ring, forced-colors fallback, real with the correct alt and width/height for 4:5. Deductions: link hrefs are relative (/work, /prints, /workshops) rather than the absolute URLs in the brief, so they break outside that domain; the web font plus font and webp preloads add first-load weight on 3G and point to files that are not present; the arrows are a muted grey and all identical.
